mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets Alloy invent a successful per-task operation whose (relationship, kind) pair is outside the permission matrix — the canonical least-privilege violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.succeeded = True and some op.target and op.kind != PostTasks and (rel[op.caller, op.target] -> op.kind) not in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clears the cross-team / in-team-no-rel denial. The injected fact then forces an outsider-success operation to exist, which any byte-equivalent / no-leakage assertion must reject.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamViolation { some op: Operation | some op.target and rel[op.caller, op.target] in (OutsiderRel + InTeamNoneRel) and op.succeeded = True }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the owner-only constraint on PatchShares lets a non-owner succeed at modifying the share list — exactly the Q1=A violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NonOwnerShares { some op: Operation | op.kind = PatchShares and op.succeeded = True and some op.target and op.caller != op.target.owner }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without this fact, successful mutations may have zero audit entries (or failed ops may emit entries). The injected violation forces a successful PATCH with no audit entry — the canonical 'state change without audit' bug.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingAudit { some op: Operation | op.succeeded = True and op.kind = PatchFields and some op.target and no op.emits }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets the audit entry's actor or role be unhooked from the calling operation — exactly the FR-002 attribution-correctness failure mode (role spoofed from body, etc.).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_BadAttribution { some op: Operation, ae: op.emits | ae.actor != op.caller or ae.actorRole != op.caller.userRole }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing 'each AuditEntry has exactly one emitting Operation' allows the same audit row to be claimed by two operations — a structural mutation/duplication of an append-only artefact.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj op1, op2: Operation | some ae: AuditEntry | ae in op1.emits and ae in op2.emits }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows a sharee whose team differs from the task's team. The injected fact forces such a cross-team share to exist, violating FR-012.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamShare { some t: Task | some u: t.sharedWith | u.userTeam != t.taskTeam }
